title: Can This Answer Lose?
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Classify eight answers, ancient and modern, as could be proven wrong, comes true either way, or not a prediction, then test each against two possible outcomes to see whether it could ever lose.

educational.topic: Hedged oracle answers and testable predictions
learningObjectives: Distinguish answers that could be proven wrong from hedged answers that come true whatever happens and from answers that are not predictions at all, classifying at least 6 of 8 answers correctly on the first attempt, including the Croesus answer and the Chaerephon answer.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Commit-then-test classification: the learner predicts a category, then a two-outcome test reveals the answer's structure
keyQuestions: Could anything that happens prove this answer wrong?
Which outcomes would make the answer come true?
Is this answer a prediction at all, or a command?
commonMisconceptions: An answer that came true must have been a good prediction.
Every oracle answer was a prediction, when many were commands.
A claim about the present cannot be tested.
A prediction that came true in a story proves the oracle's foresight.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score on eight cards (mastery: 6 of 8, with cards 1 and 4 correct).
Explain why an answer that cannot lose predicts nothing.
